items.title: Where, when, or how?
items.q: The fox hid behind the log. What does behind the log tell you?
items.why: Behind the log is a place. It tells where.

miss.1: Is behind the log a time? Think about a place.
miss.2: Is it the way the fox hid? Think about a place.

items.title: Where, when, or how?
items.q: The owl hooted at midnight. What does at midnight tell you?
items.why: Midnight is a time. It tells when.

miss.0: Can you stand at midnight? It is a time, not a place.
miss.2: It is not the way the owl hooted. Midnight is a time.

items.title: Where, when, or how?
items.q: Jemmy spoke in a whisper. What does in a whisper tell you?
items.why: In a whisper is the way he spoke. It tells how.

miss.0: A whisper is not a place. It is the way he spoke.
miss.1: A whisper is not a time. It is the way he spoke.

items.title: Find the preposition
items.q: Which word is the preposition? The boys waited until dark.
items.why: Until sits in front of dark and tells when.

miss.1: Waited is what the boys did. Look for the small word in front of dark.

items.q: A spectacle is something big and amazing, like a parade. What do people do at a spectacle?

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it’s Opti. Last week the prince said no to going home, and Jemmy talked the outlaws into sending the horse instead. Today, one outlaw rides away, and the boys are left with Cutwater. Jemmy has a plan. Will the prince help him, or not?
transcripts.guide1: Word work first. Today you’ll meet a very old root. Three words share it. See if you can figure out what it means before the page tells you. Then you’ll learn the little words that tell where, when, and how.
transcripts.guide2: Before you read: skim Chapter 11 again, since you met it last week. Then slow down for Chapter 12. Jemmy makes a plan to escape, and he needs the prince to say one thing. Watch what the prince says instead.
transcripts.guide3: Good writers prove what they say. Today, check your examples. Does each one name a chapter and tell exactly what happened? If not, add the chapter and the detail.

notes.wordParts: The root spect means “look.” inspect = look closely into, spectator = one who looks on, respect = look again with care, inspector = one whose job is to look.
notes.grammar: A preposition sits in front of a noun and ties it to the sentence. It can tell where (under the straw), when (after the storm), or how (with great care).
notes.spelling: To read a long word, find the vowels, split between them, read each beat, then push the beats together: im·por·tant.
notes.wgrd: Good readers read between the lines. When a character does not say how he feels, what he does shows it.
vocab: a small thing that is not worth much
money demanded to set a prisoner free

mods.script: Let's be word detectives. Back in Chapter 8, Billy's red eyebrows shot up in bewildered surprise. Jemmy had just shocked him. Now the parts: be, wilder, e d. Wilder is an old word for getting lost in a wild place. So bewildered means so confused you feel lost. Now tap Opti reads it on each card. Guess, then flip. Then play the matching game.

mods.todo: Tap Now check your thinking. Then sort each phrase: where, when, or how.
mods.script: Two sentences. Leaves crackled. Leaves crackled under Jemmy's feet. What did the second one add? It tells you more about the leaves, and it starts with the little word under. Under is a preposition. It sits in front of a noun and ties it to the rest of the sentence. Some prepositions tell where. Some tell when. Some tell how. Tap Now check your thinking. Say the words in Group A and Group B, and clap them. Tap See the Rule. Then sort the six words. Look at each chunk. Does one end with a vowel, like ba in bacon? Or end with a silent e, like cake?

mods.label: Opti shows you how
mods.todo: Write the sentence three new ways, one box at a time.
mods.script: [warmly] Remember copia? It means saying one idea in many ways. Watch me try one first, with a different sentence. The outlaw rode away. Box one, change the opener: Without a word, the outlaw rode away. Box two, swap the verb for a stronger one: The outlaw galloped away. Box three, add a detail: The big outlaw rode away on the king's horse. Now it's your turn, one box at a time. If you get stuck, tap Show one way.

Here's something to think about. In Chapter 11, the prince refuses to go home, and Billy pulls off his belt. Jemmy steps in with a new plan. Jemmy has every reason to let the prince suffer. So why does he keep helping him? Keep that question with you while you read.

mods.script: Time to read. You met Chapter 11 last week, so skim it to remember what happened. Then slow down for Chapter 12. First, read the two Pause and Think questions below. In Chapter 12, Jemmy makes a plan to escape, and he needs the prince to say one thing to Cutwater. Watch what the prince says instead. Stop at each question, think, and keep reading.

Two, why is Jemmy so surprised? Think about how the prince acted before. Three, is it a betrayal, or could there be another reason? For a challenge, pick Scholar, and add one more detail to each answer.

Her strong example names Chapter 2, and gives the prince's own words. Now find one example in your paragraph that needs a chapter number. Write it again with the chapter and a clear detail.

cards.bewildered: Bewildered. Hold-Your-Nose Billy's red eyebrows shot up in bewildered surprise. Bewildered means completely confused.
cards.trifle: Trifle. That crown! A trifle, scoffed Hold-Your-Nose Billy. A trifle is a small thing that is not worth much. Billy thinks a golden crown is not enough!
cards.truss: Truss. Lads, you won't mind if I truss you up like a Christmas goose. To truss someone means to tie them up tight. That's Cutwater, in Chapter 12.
cards.ransom: Ransom. The outlaws want gold from the king before they let the prince go. That gold is a ransom.

items.t: Jemmy burrows under the moldy straw so he can slip away from Cutwater.
items.why: He is in danger, but he makes a plan and carries it out.

items.t: Jemmy tells the prince, “Jemmy protects himself,” and says how he will escape.
items.why: He does not wait for someone to save him. He is ready to run.

items.t: Cutwater asks where the prince is. The prince says, “Him? Over there. Under the straw.”
items.why: He gives Jemmy away instead of helping him.
